sections.section_title: The Advantage of the Jew and the Faithfulness of God
sections.summary: Paul affirms that the Jewish advantage is real (custodianship of God's oracles) and that human unfaithfulness does not nullify God's faithfulness, which is grounded in God's own character rather than human performance.

sections.section_title: The Objection from God's Use of Human Unrighteousness
sections.summary: Paul addresses and rejects the objection that if human unrighteousness displays God's righteousness, then God is unjust to punish, dismissing the reductio ad absurdum that one should do evil so good may come.

sections.section_title: The Universal Indictment from Israel's Own Scriptures
sections.summary: Paul assembles a catena of scriptural quotations from Psalms and Isaiah demonstrating that none is righteous, none seeks God, all have turned aside, and there is no fear of God, establishing universal human sinfulness from Israel's own texts.

sections.section_title: The Function of the Law and the Closure of Every Mouth
sections.summary: Paul concludes that the law speaks to those under it so that every mouth is stopped and the whole world is accountable to God, since by works of the law no flesh will be justified, the law's function being to produce knowledge of sin.

sections.section_title: The Righteousness of God Manifested Apart from the Law
sections.summary: Paul reveals the solution: the righteousness of God manifested apart from the law, through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ for all who believe, enacted through Christ's death as the hilasterion where God is shown to be both just and the justifier of those who have faith.

sections.section_title: Boasting Excluded, One God for All
sections.summary: Paul declares boasting excluded by the principle of faith, affirms that the one God justifies both circumcised and uncircumcised through the same faith, and asserts that faith upholds rather than overthrows the law.
